claims.text: A service-level agreement is the part of a vendor's contract that states measurable promises, such as monthly availability and support response times, and what the customer gets when one is missed.

A service credit is what the vendor gives back when it misses a promise; in Gateway A's offer 10% of that month's fee, Gateway B nothing. It does not return orders the business lost, so an SLA moves little of an outage's cost onto the vendor.
A 30-day month has 43,200 minutes; 0.1% of it (99.9% availability) is 43.2 minutes, about 43; 0.5% (99.5%) is 216 minutes, 3 hours 36 minutes.

An SLA's worth depends on how availability is measured (whose view counts), what it excludes, and whether a miss pays. A vendor-side measurement sees only what reaches the vendor, so calls failing before it may not count; a measure you can check gives your own figure.
Downtime the SLA excludes does not count against the promise, so a month can have more time without the service than the percentage suggests and still meet it.

claims.text: A support response time promise says how soon the vendor answers during a serious incident, not how soon the cause is fixed; Gateway A answers within 1 hour at any time, Gateway B within 1 working day (line 63).

claims.text: SLA table: A 99.9% (~43 min), successful API calls measured gateway-side, excludes maintenance announced 72 h ahead, credit 10% of month's fee, support 1 h; B 99.5% (~3 h 36 min), status page, excludes 24 h-notice maintenance and bank incidents, no credit, 1 business day.
The evaluation file states that every figure about Gateway A and Gateway B is assumed for illustration, not from a real vendor.

The evaluation concludes the credit is only part of the fee and does not cover lost orders, and Đơn Hàng does not rely on the SLA: refund requests are accepted when the gateway fails and resent within 24 hours (YC-7, YC-10).

YC-7: a customer's refund request is accepted and answered within 2 seconds even when the gateway does not answer or errors. YC-10: when the gateway fails, the request is resent automatically for at least 24 hours before staff handle it.
The gateway is chosen in the first week of Sprint 15, before the refund job is written.
Payments has a timeout, a circuit breaker and retries for gateway calls; an open circuit keeps a due refund pending to retry later.

claims.text: An SLA only says how much failure the vendor may have and what it then owes; it does not stop a single call from hanging or failing, so client-side timeouts and retries are still needed.

Try it: with Gateway A, 30 min of maintenance announced 4 days ahead is excluded; if A's own record shows the 25-min outage, 25 minutes count, under 43, so no credit; missed calls lower the count. B also excludes the maintenance (24 h notice), counts by its status page, pays no credit.
